ground_truth.description: _claimFees() sweeps the entire balance of `token0`/`token1` after `collectFees()`, stealing rewards if `rewardToken` matches `token0` or `token1`. Impact: Bribe contract receives staking rewards instead of fees.
ground_truth.root_cause: _claimFees() sweeps the entire balance of `token0`/`token1` after `collectFees()`, stealing rewards if `rewardToken` matches `token0` or `token1`. Impact: Bribe contract receives staking rewards instead of fees.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: A test deposits 10 HYBR rewards, adds 0.1 HYBR fees, and `claimFees()` sweeps all 10.1 HYBR to the bribe contract.
ground_truth.fix_description: Transfer only the difference in balance before/after `collectFees()`; add access control to `claimFees`. Status: Mitigation confirmed.

vulnerabilities.explanation: After clPool.collectFees(), _claimFees reads the entire token0/token1 balanceOf(address(this)) and forwards it to internal_bribe. It does not track the delta from collectFees, so any rewardToken already present (or arriving via notifyRewardAmount) is swept if rewardToken == token0 or token1.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. rewardToken equals token0. 2. notifyRewardAmount sends rewards to GaugeCL. 3. Attacker calls claimFees() (permissionless). 4. All rewardToken balance is approved and sent to bribe via notifyRewardAmount instead of staying for stakers.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Record balances before collectFees, compute only the delta, and transfer that amount. Add access control (onlyDistribution or similar) to claimFees.

prediction.overall_explanation: The root cause is the unconditional full-balance transfer in _claimFees after collectFees. This allows theft of rewardToken holdings when token overlap occurs. The function is callable by anyone.
